filer-mennonite-filer-id.assessment: Filer Mennonite Church is the lone CMC/Rosedale Network congregation in Idaho, anchoring conservative Anabaptist witness in the Magic Valley region of southern Idaho. Pastor Ronald D. Hershey leads. The Rosedale Network (formerly Conservative Mennonite Conference) practices male-only ordination, plural-male-elder polity, and adheres to the historic Dordrecht Confession alongside its own Statement of Theology. This gives Filer Mennonite real confessional accountability and a clearly complementarian polity, distinguishing it from the more progressive Mennonite Church USA. Green rating reflects the conservative Anabaptist denomination's strong gender, leadership, and confessional integrity.

first-african-baptist-richmond.assessment: First African Baptist Church of Richmond is one of the most historically significant Black churches in the United States — founded in 1841 from the Black members of Richmond's First Baptist Church, at a time when both enslaved and free Black Christians gathered to worship. The church has been a spiritual anchor in Richmond's Black community through slavery, Reconstruction, Jim Crow, and the Civil Rights movement. Dr. Rodney D. Waller is the 10th Senior Pastor, serving for 16+ years and described as an 'anointed' preacher with deep community roots. The theological concerns are the standard ones for NBC/BGAV churches: no formal inerrancy requirement, women in ministry permitted, and the ever-present tension in historically Black mainline churches between prophetic social justice and Gospel proclamation. USMC Ministries should approach with respect for the extraordinary historical legacy while verifying current doctrinal commitments. This church is a kingdom partner candidate for outreach even if full theological alignment is uncertain.

For anyone in the Kenedy area, visiting this congregation and directly inquiring about leadership structure and doctrinal commitments is the recommended path.

first-baptist-church-richmond-city.assessment: First Baptist Church (City) on Monument Avenue is one of Richmond's oldest and most historic Baptist congregations, founded in 1780. However, it is aligned with the Cooperative Baptist Fellowship — the progressive wing of Baptist life that rejected the SBC conservative resurgence. CBF churches typically reject strict inerrancy, affirm women's ordination at all levels, and increasingly affirm LGBTQ+ inclusion. While the history is remarkable, the current theological trajectory has moved significantly away from conservative evangelical convictions. Not recommended for those seeking inerrantist, complementarian Baptist worship.

first-baptist-hammond-in.assessment: First Baptist Hammond is one of the most controversial churches in American Christianity. Founded 1887, it became a megachurch under Jack Hyles. The church has been plagued by scandals: Jack Schaap (Hyles' successor and son-in-law) was convicted of transporting a minor across state lines for sexual activity (2012). Multiple staff/associated pastors have faced similar charges. The institutional culture has been widely criticized for prioritizing numbers, easy-believism, and personality-driven leadership over genuine accountability. Current pastor John Wilkerson has attempted to restore credibility, but the institutional DNA remains a major concern. NOT recommended without extensive personal investigation.

first-baptist-hammond-in-ifb.assessment: First Baptist Church of Hammond is the historic Hyles-Anderson legacy IFB congregation in Hammond, IN. The church is tied to Hyles-Anderson College and was led by Jack Hyles from 1959 until his death in 2001, then by his son-in-law Jack Schaap from 2001 until Schaap's 2012 conviction for sexual misconduct with a 16-year-old church member (he served prison time and was released 2021). Multiple women have publicly described abuse and cover-up patterns spanning decades of the Hyles era. Current senior pastor John Wilkerson (since 2013) inherited the institution at its lowest reputational point and has publicly acknowledged the failures while leading reform. The congregation is included for completeness as one of the most consequential IFB institutions in the country, but is rated YELLOW with significant caution: the documented abuse history, Hyles-era pastor-as-king theology, and KJV-Only doctrinal emphasis all warrant discernment. Adam should not visit casually; survivors of Hyles/Schaap-era abuse remain a live pastoral concern within IFB circles.

Patriarchal complementarian leadership default. Visit with discernment — GARBC churches often score better than typical IFB on translation and exposition while retaining traditional gender roles.

first-baptist-newport-news.assessment: First Baptist Church Newport News has a remarkable 140-year history on the Virginia Peninsula, organized in 1881 and formally constituted in 1883. Dr. Randy Shepley III leads this historic congregation. The concern is the BGAV affiliation — the Baptist General Association of Virginia is the moderate Baptist body in Virginia, distinct from the more conservative SBC of Virginia. BGAV is connected with the Cooperative Baptist Fellowship and takes a theologically moderate stance that allows greater diversity on Scripture, gender roles, and cultural issues than the SBC's Baptist Faith & Message 2000. This doesn't make FBCNN a bad church — but it means verification is required. Visit, listen to the preaching, ask directly about their stance on Scripture's authority and complementarian convictions before committing. The historic pedigree is impressive; the denominational framework is less clearly conservative.

score_notes.scripture: BGAV does not require inerrancy — while many congregations hold to biblical authority, the denominational framework is more theologically moderate than the SBC's Baptist Faith & Message 2000.

score_notes.mens_discipleship: Men's ministry and discipleship infrastructure needs direct verification given BGAV's more moderate denominational context.

first-baptist-san-antonio.assessment: First Baptist San Antonio is a historic downtown SBC church (est. ~1861) led by Senior Pastor Chris Johnson. Doctrinally strong: affirms Jesus as co-equal with the Father, Scripture as God's Word and 'supreme and final source of truth,' and salvation as God's free gift through personal faith in Christ. Notable strength: dedicated men's ministry ('Fearlessly Following Jesus') and a unique Bible study integration model where the same passage is studied across all ministries. The church broadcasts on KSAT-12 television, suggesting substantive preaching. One concern: women hold 'Minister' titles (Megan Langan, Tera Kouba), which goes beyond traditional complementarian support roles while stopping short of 'Pastor' titles. The senior pastoral role remains male. Extensive ministry portfolio including Spanish and Asian/international outreach. Worth deeper evaluation — one of the stronger SBC churches in the directory with solid doctrine and intentional discipleship.

score_notes.christology: Affirms Jesus as 'the Son of God and co-equal with the Father,' both human and divine, who 'arose from the dead after three days' and will return 'personally and visibly to earth.' Orthodox Christology.

score_notes.gender: Senior Pastor Chris Johnson (male). However, the church has women in ministerial titles: Megan Langan serves as 'Minister for Single Adults; Pastoral Care & Women's Ministry' and Tera Kouba as 'Minister of International/Asian Ministries.' Women hold 'Minister' titles — this goes beyond support roles. Yellow: not egalitarian in senior pastoral role but allows women ministerial titles.
score_notes.leadership: Senior pastor model with Chris Johnson. Staff of approximately 44 across ministerial, administrative, business, and facilities departments. 12 ministerial staff. References a 'lead team.' No visible elder board structure on website.
score_notes.soteriology: Clear grace-alone position: 'Salvation is God's free gift out of His grace to us' and comes 'only by personally trusting in Jesus Christ as God's offer of forgiveness.' Sound soteriology.
score_notes.cultural: No explicit DEI/CRT language detected. Church emphasizes Bible study integration across all ministries (same passage studied in Sunday School, worship, and small groups called 'Circles of Six'). Historic downtown church. Needs in-person evaluation.

first-methodist-waco-tx-gmc.assessment: First Methodist Church of Waco is a historic 1859 congregation that was among the earliest to leave the UMC and join the Global Methodist Church in 2022. Rev. Dr. Mike Voigts became Senior Pastor in May 2025 after serving as a professor at Asbury Theological Seminary — bringing academic Wesleyan depth to the pulpit. The church operates three campuses: the Main Campus on Cobbs Drive, the Speegleville Campus, and a Baylor Campus specifically reaching university students with a Tuesday 7 PM service. One flag worth noting: Rev. Dr. Blossom Matthews serves as Senior Associate Pastor, meaning this particular GMC church does appoint women to pastoral roles (distinct from formal elder ordination, which varies by conference). This places the church closer to the YELLOW end of the gender-rubric for readers committed to male-only ordination. For those comfortable with women in teaching/associate roles but male senior leadership, it's a solid orthodox Wesleyan option in Central Texas.

first-presbyterian-columbia-sc-arp.assessment: First Presbyterian Church of Columbia, South Carolina (ARP) is one of the most historically significant orthodox Reformed congregations in the United States. The 1854 church building is on the National Register of Historic Places (added January 1971). The pulpit lineage includes James Henley Thornwell, Benjamin Morgan Palmer, John Girardeau, and more recently Sinclair Ferguson and Derek Thomas — a roll call of Reformed theological heavyweights. The congregation principled-seceded from the mainline Presbyterian Church in the United States in 1983 and joined the ARP to preserve its confessional identity. Dr. Neil C. Stewart currently serves as Senior Minister and Head of Staff. Three Sunday services (8:30 AM, 11:15 AM, and 6:00 PM). ARP confessional framework with male-only ordination aligns with MOOP's biblical-design rubric. One of the strongest possible green-rated Reformed Presbyterian options in the Southeast, though note that the church's website currently displays 'Presbyterian Church (USA)' in some metadata — this appears to be outdated website text; per the ARP official directory and Wikipedia, the church has been ARP since 1983.

first-presbyterian-orlando-fl-epc.assessment: First Presbyterian Church of Orlando is a 135+ year historic congregation that voted to join the Evangelical Presbyterian Church (EPC) in 2012, departing the progressive PCUSA. For green-eligibility, verify the local elder board composition and the Central Florida Presbytery stance. Overall a solidly orthodox Reformed option in central Florida.

The PCA churches in Richmond (Third Church, City Church, River City Church) represent what the PCUSA abandoned. Not recommended.

first-umc-millville-nj.assessment: First United Methodist Church Millville is a historic Methodist congregation in South Jersey where Pastor Jack Fosbenner serves as Deacon. Jack's background is notable: 13 years as a NJ State Trooper, 12 years as Director of Camp Edge, business owner, doctorate from Seton Hall, and Deacon studies at Palmer Theological Seminary. Married to Sue for 43 years. He helps oversee the Trinity First Hope Center — a community mission ministry serving Millville. Personal friend of MOOP. The UMC denominational affiliation is the main yellow flag — post-2024 General Conference the denomination lifted restrictions on LGBTQ ordination and same-sex marriage, so individual congregations vary significantly. This particular church needs in-person evaluation to determine its specific theological posture. Jack's traditional/conservative background suggests the local culture may be more conservative than the national UMC trajectory.

first-united-methodist-midland-tx.assessment: First United Methodist Church in Midland, Texas was founded in 1885 — the first congregation organized in Midland. On November 5, 1977, 31-year-old future President George W. Bush married 31-year-old Laura Welch at this church's Glass Memorial Chapel; the Glass Chapel was completed in 1976, just a year before the wedding. The Bush wedding gives this church its primary national notability. Current senior pastor is Dr. Tim Walker, with Rev. Kurt Borden as associate. Like Highland Park UMC Dallas, First Methodist Midland stayed within the post-2024 United Methodist Church after the conservative Global Methodist Church disaffiliation wave. Per MOOP rubric this is RED at the denominational level given the post-2024 UMC departure from biblical authority on sexual ethics. Included for situational awareness about the wedding site of a former president and first lady.
